name: Email to an outside address
why: The agent tried to email a domain outside the company. This is the signature of data exfiltration by email.
response: Read the blocked event. Confirm no customer data left, and look at what the agent was asked to do just before.

name: Tool call blocked by policy
why: A defense refused a tool call. A single block is worth a look; a burst is someone probing what they can do.
response: Read the reason on the event. Repeated blocks from one user suggest a compromised session or an injection.

name: Unapproved (outside) tool used
why: The agent called a tool that did not ship with it, meaning one loaded from an outside plugin server.
response: Check which plugin the tool came from and what it did with the arguments it received.

name: File path left the workspace
why: A file read used a path that points outside the workspace: a path-traversal attempt.
response: A legitimate request never needs '..' or an absolute path. Treat as an attack.

name: Agent ran code
why: The agent executed code. Code execution is the most powerful tool; every use is worth recording.
response: Confirm the code ran in the sandbox. Review what the snippet was asked to compute.

name: Burst of tool calls in one chat
why: One request drove an unusually long run of tool calls, which can mean a loop or an agent being driven by an attacker.
response: Read the chat's tool list. A long, repetitive run is the signature of excessive agency.

name: Junior user read customer contacts
why: A junior user's session queried customer contact details. Starts disabled: it is noisy if juniors legitimately handle their own accounts.
response: Confirm per-user data access is on, so the query only returned the user's own accounts.

name: Blocked web fetch
why: The agent tried to fetch a host that is not on the allowlist, a sign of an exfiltration or recon attempt through a URL.
response: Check the host in the event. A blocked fetch to an unknown host during a normal task points to an injection.
